rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Baghawī records the explanation that Khidr added لك because Moses had broken their agreement twice.
rows.anchor: لأنه نقض العهد مرتين وفي القصة

rows.speaker: القصة
rows.claim: In the story, Joshua repeatedly reminded Moses to remember the commitment he had made.
rows.anchor: وفي القصة أن يوشع كان يقول لموسى

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads تصحبني without the alif, from the verb for companionship.
rows.anchor: وفارقني وقرأ يعقوب: " فلا تصحبني " بغير ألف من الصحبة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Abū Bakr lighten the nūn in لدني; the other readers geminate it.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو بكر " من لدني " خفيفة النون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains Moses to mean that he had excused himself between them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أي قد أعذرت فيما بيني وبينك.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that Moses had been warned he would not manage patience with Khidr.
rows.anchor: وقيل: حذرتني أني لا أستطيع معك صبرا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Moses had now made his excuse for separation clear.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اتضح لك العذر في مفارقتي.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb transmits the Prophet's prayer for mercy on Moses and himself: Moses hurried, and patience would have let him witness more wonders.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن أبي بن كعب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "رحمة الله علينا وعلى موسى"

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the town as Antioch.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يعني: "أنطاكية"

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sīrīn identifies it as al-Ubulla and calls it the place farthest from the sky.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: هي "الأبلة" وهي أبعد الأرض من السماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reported identification of the town is Barqa.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "برقة". وعن أبي هريرة:

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra identifies the town as a place in al-Andalus.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة: بلدة بالأندلس

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubayy reports the Prophet's description of the town's people as vile: the travelers went around its gatherings seeking food and were refused hospitality.
rows.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "حتى إذا أتيا أهل قرية لئاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses and Khidr toured the town asking for food and lodging, but its people gave them neither.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهما طافا في القرية فاستطعماهم فلم يطعموهما

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda calls a village that refuses guests the worst kind of village.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: شر القرى التي لا تضيف الضيف.

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abū Hurayra says a Berber woman fed them after the men refused; they prayed for the women and cursed the men.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي هريرة قال: أطعمتهما امرأة من أهل بربر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wall's wanting to collapse is figurative: it means it was near falling, since a wall cannot literally intend anything; Arabs similarly say one house looks toward another when they face each other.
rows.anchor: وهذا من مجاز كلام العرب لأن الجدار لا إرادة له وإنما معناه: قرب ودنا من السقوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أقامه means Khidr straightened or set the wall upright.
rows.anchor: {فأقامه} أي سواه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ubayy reports from the Prophet that Khidr raised the wall with his hand.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال الخضر بيده فأقامه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Khidr wiped the wall with his hand and it stood straight.
rows.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: مسح الجدار بيده فاستقام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Khidr first demolished the wall, then sat and rebuilt it.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: هدمه ثم قعد يبنيه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says Khidr plastered the wall and built it up.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: بل طينا وجعل يبني الحائط.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb read لتخذت with a light t and kasra on kh; the others read it with a doubled t and fatḥa, two Arabic forms like اتبع and تبع.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: "لتخذت" بتخفيف التاء وكسر الخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عليه refers to taking payment for repairing the wall.
rows.anchor: {عليه} يعني على إصلاح الجدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means that, since they were hungry and the townspeople had not fed them, Khidr could have charged for his work.
rows.anchor: معناه: إنك قد علمت أننا جياع وأن أهل القرية لم يطعمونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr says this is now the time for them to part.
rows.anchor: يعني هذا وقت فراق بيني وبينك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Moses' objection to leaving the wall without payment caused their separation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا الإنكار على ترك الأجر هو المفرق بيننا.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as separation from their companionship, with بين repeated for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: معناه هذا فراق بيننا أي فراق اتصالنا وكرر "بين" تأكيدا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سأنبئك means that Khidr will soon inform Moses.
rows.anchor: {سأنبئك} أي سوف أخبرك

rows.speaker: بعض التفاسير
rows.claim: Some commentaries say Moses grabbed Khidr's garment and asked him to explain his earlier actions before leaving; Khidr began with the ship.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض التفاسير أن موسى أخذ بثوبه فقال: أخبرني بمعنى ما عملت

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the ship belonged to ten brothers: five disabled and five who worked at sea.
rows.anchor: قال كعب: كانت لعشرة إخوة خمسة زمنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that someone may own property yet still be called poor when it does not meet their needs.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن المسكين وإن كان يملك شيئا فلا يزول عنه اسم المسكنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The owners worked at sea by hiring out the ship and earning from it.
rows.anchor: {يعملون في البحر} أي: يؤاجرون ويكتسبون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعيبها means that Khidr intended to make the ship defective.
rows.anchor: {فأردت أن أعيبها} أجعلها ذات عيب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī takes وراءهم to mean ahead of them, citing the same usage in 14:16 and Ibn ʿAbbās's reading أمامهم.
rows.anchor: {وكان وراءهم} أي أمامهم {ملك} كقوله: "من ورائه جهنم" (إبراهيم-16)

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes وراءهم as behind them, since the king lay on their return route; Baghawī prefers ahead.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "وراءهم" خلفهم وكان رجوعهم في طريقهم عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads that the king seized every sound ship by force; Khidr damaged this one to keep it from him.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقرأ كذلك فخرقها وعيبها الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king was called al-Julandī and was an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: وكان اسمه الجلندي وكان كافرا.

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq gives the king's name as Mutawallih ibn Jalandi al-Azdī.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق: اسمه "متوله بن جلندي الأزدي".

rows.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
rows.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbāʾī gives the king's name as Hudad ibn Badad.
rows.anchor: وقال شعيب الجبائي: اسمه "هدد بن بدد"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Khidr later explained the king's threat to the uninformed owners so they could repair the ship after he passed it.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الخضر اعتذر إلى القوم وذكر لهم شأن الملك الغاصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship's damage was repaired either by plugging it with a small vessel or by using tar.
rows.anchor: قيل: سدوها بقارورة وقيل: بالقار.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Baghawī explains فخشينا as فَعَلِمنا and notes Ibn ʿAbbās's reading that the boy was an unbeliever while his parents were believers.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن عباس: "وأما الغلام فكان كافرا وكان أبواه مؤمنين فخشينا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يرهقهما means that the boy would overwhelm or cover his parents.
rows.anchor: {أن يرهقهما} يغشيهما

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses يرهقهما as making the parents bear or incur something.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يكلفهما

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says Khidr feared the parents' love for the boy would lead them to follow his religion.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: فخشينا أن يحملهما حبه على أن يتابعاه على دينه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and Abū ʿAmr read يبدلهما with doubling; the remaining readers lighten it, and both forms are valid Arabic.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ونافع وأبو عمرو: بالتشديد هاهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinguish the forms: tabdīl changes an object's state while it remains, whereas ibdāl removes one thing and puts another in its place.
rows.anchor: وفرق بعضهم فقال: "التبديل": تغيير الشيء أو تغيير حاله وعين الشيء قائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خيرا منه زكاة means a replacement better in righteousness and piety.
rows.anchor: {ربهما خيرا منه زكاة} أي صلاحا وتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Jaʿfar, and Yaʿqūb pronounce the ḥāʾ of رحما with ḍamma; the others use sukūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر ويعقوب: بضم الحاء والباقون بجزمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رحما can mean compassion from mercy or kinship.
rows.anchor: أي: عطفا من الرحمة. وقيل: هو من الرحم والقرابة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains the replacement as closer kin and more dutiful to the parents.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أي أوصل للرحم وأبر بوالديه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says God replaced the boy with a girl who married a prophet and bore a prophet through whom a nation was guided.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: أبدلهما الله جارية فتزوجها نبي من الأنبياء فولدت له نبيا

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, transmitting from his father, says the replacement girl bore seventy prophets.
rows.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه قال: أبدلهما الله جارية ولدت سبعين نبيا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says God replaced the boy with another boy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: أبدلهما بغلام

rows.speaker: مطرف
rows.claim: Muṭarrif says the parents rejoiced at the boy's birth and grieved at his death; had he lived he would have ruined them, so a believer should accept God's decree, since what one dislikes may be better.
rows.anchor: قال مطرف: فرح به أبواه حين ولد وحزنا عليه حين قتل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two orphan boys are said to have been named Aṣram and Ṣarīm.
rows.anchor: وكان اسمهما أصرم وصريم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abū al-Dardāʾ attributes to the Prophet that the treasure was gold and silver.
rows.anchor: روي عن أبي الدرداء عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: "كان ذهبا وفضة"

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the treasure was wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: كان مالا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the treasure was scrolls containing knowledge.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير: كان الكنز صحفا فيها علم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it was a golden tablet bearing maxims about death, judgment, provision, destiny, and the world's transience, plus testimony to God's oneness and the creation of good and evil.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: أنه قال كان لوحا من ذهب مكتوبا فيه: "عجبا لمن أيقن بالموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī says most exegetes accept Ibn ʿAbbās's tablet account and that it is also transmitted as a Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أكثر المفسرين (4) وروي ذلك مرفوعا.

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says bare كنز normally means money, though a qualified phrase can mean a treasure of knowledge; this tablet combined both.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: الكنز إذا أطلق ينصرف إلى كنز المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous father was reportedly named Kāsiḥ and was among the devout.
rows.anchor: قيل: كان اسمه "كاسح" وكان من الأتقياء.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the boys were protected because of their parents' righteousness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حفظا بصلاح أبويهما.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report places seven generations between the boys and their righteous ancestor.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان بينهما وبين الأب الصالح سبعة آباء

rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir says God protects a righteous servant's children, descendants, clan, and nearby households for as long as righteousness remains among them.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن المنكدر: إن الله يحفظ بصلاح العبد ولده

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says that when he remembers his children while praying, he lengthens his prayer.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: إني لأصلي فأذكر ولدي فأزيد في صلاتي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys reaching their أشد can mean attaining understanding, reaching physical strength, or reaching eighteen years.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أن يدركا شدتهما وقوتهما. وقيل: ثمان عشرة سنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once mature, the boys would extract their treasure; رحمة here means a blessing from God.
rows.anchor: {ويستخرجا} حينئذ {كنزهما رحمة} نعمة {من ربك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr says his actions came from God's command and inspiration, not his own choice or judgment.
rows.anchor: أي باختياري ورأيي بل فعلته بأمر الله وإلهامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اسطاع and استطاع have the same meaning: Moses could not endure the matter.
rows.anchor: أي لم تطق عليه صبرا و"استطاع" و"اسطاع" بمعنى واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses asked Khidr for advice before parting; Khidr told him to seek knowledge in order to act on it, not merely to recount it.
rows.anchor: روي أن موسى لما أراد أن يفارقه قال له: أوصني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view holds that Khidr and Elijah remain alive and meet each year during pilgrimage season.
rows.anchor: قيل: إن الخضر وإلياس حيان يلتقيان كل سنة بالموسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Khidr drank from the life spring when Dhu al-Qarnayn entered the darkness seeking it; Dhu al-Qarnayn lost the way back.
rows.anchor: وكان سبب حياته فيما يحكى أنه شرب من عين الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say Khidr is dead, citing 21:34 and the Prophet's report after the night prayer that none then alive would remain a century later.
rows.anchor: وذهب آخرون إلى أنه ميت لقوله تعالى: "وما جعلنا لبشر من قبلك الخلد" (الأنبياء-34)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some scholars say Dhu al-Qarnayn was a prophet.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كان نبيا

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: In Abū al-Ṭufayl's report, ʿAlī says Dhu al-Qarnayn was neither prophet nor king, but a servant who loved and was loved by God and sincerely advised Him.
rows.anchor: قال: لم يكن نبيا ولا ملكا ولكن كان عبدا أحب الله وأحبه الله

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar rebuked someone for calling another man Dhu al-Qarnayn, saying people had taken names of prophets and now even names of angels.
rows.anchor: وروي أن عمر رضي الله عنه سمع رجلا يقول لآخر: يا ذا القرنين فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars hold that Dhu al-Qarnayn was a just and righteous king.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه كان ملكا عادلا صالحا

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī says he was named Dhu al-Qarnayn because he reached the sun's two horns, its east and west.
rows.anchor: قال الزهري: لأنه بلغ قرني الشمس مشرقها ومغربها.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another etymology says he ruled the Romans and Persians.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه ملك الروم وفارس.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another etymology says he entered light and darkness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه دخل النور والظلمة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says he dreamed that he grasped the two horns of the sun.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه رأى في المنام كأنه أخذ بقرني الشمس.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account derives the name from his two handsome locks of hair.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كانت له ذؤابتان حسنتان.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says he had two horns concealed beneath his turban.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لأنه كان له قرنان تواريهما العمامة.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī says he was named after his people struck one horn when he urged piety, then struck the other after God revived him and he urged them again.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو الطفيل عن علي أنه [قال سمي "ذا القرنين" لأنه] (3) أمر قومه بتقوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view names him Marzbān ibn Marzaba, a Greek descendant of Yūnān ibn Yāfith ibn Noah.
rows.anchor: قيل: اسمه "مرزبان بن مرزبة اليوناني" من ولد يونان بن يافث بن نوح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view names him Alexander ibn Philip, the Roman.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اسمه "الإسكندر بن فيلفوس بن ياملوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's enabling Dhu al-Qarnayn means establishing him in the land and preparing the means for him.
rows.anchor: أوطأنا، والتمكين: تمهيد الأسباب.

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī describes his enabling as clouds carrying him, means opened to him, light spread before him, and night and day becoming equal, making travel easy.
rows.anchor: قال علي: سخر له السحاب فحمله عليها، ومد له في الأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave him everything people need.
rows.anchor: {وآتيناه من كل شيء} أي: أعطيناه من كل شيء يحتاج إليه الخلق.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that he received everything kings need to conquer cities and fight enemies.
rows.anchor: وقيل: من كل ما يستعين به الملوك على فتح المدن ومحاربة الأعداء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sabab is a means or knowledge by which he could reach what he wanted and travel across the earth.
rows.anchor: والسبب: ما يوصل الشيء إلى الشيء.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses sabab as reaching wherever he wished.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: بلاغا إلى حيث أراد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says the earth's regions were brought near to him.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قربنا إليه أقطار الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readers of the Ḥijāz and Basra connect and double the form اتبع; the others separate the hamza and use a still t.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الحجاز، والبصرة: "فاتبع" و"ثم اتبع" موصولا مشددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some treat the readings as synonymous, Baghawī distinguishes them: the separated form means catching up, while the doubled form means traveling behind someone.
rows.anchor: والصحيح: الفرق بينهما، فمن قطع الألف فمعناه: أدرك ولحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here sabab means a route, while Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as a stopping place.
rows.anchor: وقوله: "سببا" أي: طريقا. وقال ابن عباس: منزلا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Abū ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr read حامية, meaning hot; the others read حمئة, meaning muddy.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وأبو عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر: " حامية " بالألف غير مهموزة

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: When Muʿāwiya asked what the Torah says about sunset, Kaʿb answered that it sets in water and mud.
rows.anchor: وسأل معاوية كعبا: كيف تجد في التوراة أن تغرب الشمس؟

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybī says in the muddy spring may mean at a muddy spring, or describe how it appears to the eye.
rows.anchor: قال القتيبي: يجوز أن يكون معنى قوله: {في عين حمئة} أي: عندها عين حمئة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj describes the people near the spring as living in a city with twelve thousand gates; its silence would let one hear the sun's setting thud.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جريج: مدينة لها اثنا عشر ألف باب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's address to Dhu al-Qarnayn is used to argue he was a prophet, but Baghawī says the sounder view is that he was not and received inspiration.
rows.anchor: يستدل بهذا من زعم أنه كان نبيا فإن الله تعالى خاطبه والأصح: أنه لم يكن نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn's option to punish means killing those who do not enter Islam.
rows.anchor: {إما أن تعذب} يعني: إما أن تقتلهم إن لم يدخلوا في الإسلام

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Taking goodness among them can mean pardoning them, or capturing them to teach them guidance.
rows.anchor: وقيل: تأسرهم فتعلمهم الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ظلم means disbelief, and Dhu al-Qarnayn's immediate punishment is killing; in the afterlife the unbeliever is returned to God for Hell, worse than killing.
rows.anchor: {قال أما من ظلم} أي: كفر {فسوف نعذبه} أي: نقتله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ḥafṣ, and Yaʿqūb read جزاء in the accusative with nunation as a verbal noun in place of a circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب: {جزاء} منصوبا منونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other readers use nominative construction; الحسنى then means Paradise, as in the cited phrase about the Hereafter being better.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون: بالرفع على الإضافة، فالحسنى: الجنة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation of الحسنى in the nominative reading is righteous deeds, whose reward the believer receives.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد ب "الحسنى" على هذه القراءة: الأعمال الصالحة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will speak gently to the righteous believer and treat him with ease; Mujāhid glosses يسرا as kind treatment.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: "يسرا" أي: معروفا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following another sabab means traveling along routes and stopping places.
rows.anchor: {ثم أتبع سببا} أي: سلك طرقا ومنازل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sunrise point is a place where the sun rises.
rows.anchor: {حتى إذا بلغ مطلع الشمس} أي موضع طلوعها

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḥasan say the people had no shelter from the sun; because buildings could not stand there, they lived in burrows until it passed and then came out to work their fields.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والحسن: لم يكن بينهم وبين الشمس ستر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan also says they entered water at sunrise and emerged to graze like animals once the sun had risen above them.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: كانوا إذا طلعت الشمس يدخلون الماء

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī describes them as naked, using one ear as a bed and the other as a covering.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: هم قوم عراة يفترش أحدهم إحدى أذنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كذلك may mean that Dhu al-Qarnayn reached east as he had reached west; Baghawī prefers that he judged the eastern people as he had judged the western people.
rows.anchor: قيل: معناه كما بلغ مغرب الشمس كذلك بلغ مطلعها والصحيح أن معناه: كما حكم في القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God fully knew what Dhu al-Qarnayn had with him, including his troops, equipment, and tools.
rows.anchor: يعني: بما عنده ومعه (3) من الجند والعدة والآلات "خبرا" أي: علما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ open the sīn in السدين; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī also open it in سدا here, while other readings use ḍamma.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وحفص: {السدين} و" سدا " هاهنا بفتح السين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some say the two vowel forms of سد mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: منهم من قال: هما لغتان معناهما واحد.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima, also reported from Abū ʿAmr, says the open-vowel form is human-made and the ḍamma form is made by God.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: ما كان من صنعة بني آدم فهو السد بالفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the two سدّين are mountains, between which Dhu al-Qarnayn built a barrier against Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "السد": بالفتح مصدر وبالضم اسم وهما هاهنا: جبلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read يفقهون with a passive sense, meaning the people cannot make others understand them; the others read it as their inability to understand others.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: "يفقهون" بضم الياء وكسر القاف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they understood nobody's speech and other people could not understand them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا يفقهون كلام أحد ولا يفهم الناس كلامهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A translator could have spoken for them; Ibn Masʿūd's reading supports this by explicitly introducing the people around them as speakers.
rows.anchor: قيل: كلم عنهم مترجم، دليله: قراءة ابن مسعود:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim reads Yaʾjūj and Maʾjūj with two hamzas, while the others omit hamza; both readings recur in 21:96.
rows.anchor: قرأهما عاصم بهمزتين [وكذلك في الأنبياء، "فتحت يأجوج ومأجوج"]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One etymology derives their names from the blazing of fire, likening their numbers and intensity to its flare; another treats them as foreign names like Hārūt and Mārūt.
rows.anchor: وهما لغتان أصلهما من أجيج النار وهو ضوؤها وشررها شبهوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are said to descend from Yāfith son of Noah.
rows.anchor: وهم من أولاد يافث بن نوح

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk calls them a people of the Turks.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك: هم جيل من الترك.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the Turks were a detachment of Gog and Magog left outside when Dhu al-Qarnayn built the barrier.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: الترك سرية من يأجوج ومأجوج، خرجت فضرب ذو القرنين السد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says they were twenty-two tribes; the barrier enclosed twenty-one, leaving one outside, the Turks, whose name means those left behind.
rows.anchor: وعن قتادة: أنهم اثنان وعشرون قبيلة

rows.speaker: أهل التواريخ
rows.claim: Historians divide Noah's descendants among Shem, Ham, and Yāfith, assigning Arabs and Romans to Shem, Africans to Ham, and Turks, Khazars, Slavs, and Gog and Magog to Yāfith.
rows.anchor: قال أهل التواريخ: أولاد نوح ثلاثة سام وحام ويافث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the transmission of ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās says Gog and Magog form ten portions while all other children of Adam are one portion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: هم عشرة أجزاء وولد آدم كلهم جزء.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa's marfūʿ report says each of Gog and Magog comprises four hundred thousand communities; a man lives to see a thousand armed male descendants, and they will ruin the world.
rows.anchor: روي عن حذيفة مرفوعا: إن يأجوج أمة ومأجوج أمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account describes three kinds: a cedar-tall kind, a square kind impervious to mountains and iron, and a kind that covers itself with its ears and eats beasts and the dead; their masses range from Syria to Khurasan and drink eastern rivers and Lake Tiberias.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هم ثلاثة أصناف، صنف منهم أمثال الأرز شجر بالشام

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says some are a handspan tall and others are excessively tall.
rows.anchor: وعن علي أنه قال: منهم من طوله شبر ومنهم من هو

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb gives an unusual origin account: Adam's nocturnal emission mixed with earth, so Gog and Magog descend from him through the father but not the mother.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: هم نادرة في ولد آدم وذلك أن آدم احتلم ذات يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story describes them as uniformly half a man's height, with claws, predatory teeth, body hair, and huge ears used as bedding and cover; they mate like animals. Dhu al-Qarnayn then dug to water and filled the foundation with stone and clay, pouring melted copper into it.
rows.anchor: ولكل واحد منهم أذنان عظيمتان يفترش إحداهما ويلتحف بالأخرى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says they damaged the land by eating all greenery and carrying off dry goods, causing severe injury and killing people.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: فسادهم أنهم كانوا يخرجون أيام الربيع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says their corruption consisted of eating people.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فسادهم أنهم كانوا يأكلون الناس.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they will spread corruption when they emerge.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه أنهم سيفسدون في الأرض عند خروجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read خراجا with an alif while the others read خرجا; both mean payment or a fee from their wealth.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي " خراجا " بالألف وقرأ الآخرون {خرجا}

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguishes voluntary payment, kharj, from obligatory payment, kharāj.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو: "الخرج": ما تبرعت به و"الخراج": ما لزمك أداؤه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another distinction assigns kharāj to land and kharj to persons or heads.
rows.anchor: وقيل: "الخراج": على الأرض و"الخرج": على الرقاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed barrier was to keep Gog and Magog from reaching the people.
rows.anchor: {على أن تجعل بيننا وبينهم سدا} أي حاجزا فلا يصلون إلينا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads مكنني with two explicit nūns; the other readers assimilate them into one doubled nūn.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير " مكنني " بنونين ظاهرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn says God's empowerment of him is better than the payment they offered.
rows.anchor: أي: ما قواني عليه {ربي خير} من جعلكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not want money: he asks them to help with their bodies and strength.
rows.anchor: معناه: إني لا أريد المال بل أعينوني بأبدانكم وقوتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ridm is a barrier; when asked what help he needed, he requested skilled builders, workers, and tools.
rows.anchor: قالوا وما تلك القوة؟ قال: فعلة وصناع يحسنون البناء والعمل والآلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آتوني means give me; Abū Bakr reads ائتوني, meaning bring me.
rows.anchor: {آتوني} أعطوني وقرأ أبو بكر: " ائتوني " أي جيئوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zubar are pieces of iron; the people supplied iron and firewood, which Dhu al-Qarnayn layered until the gap between the slopes was level.
rows.anchor: {زبر الحديد} أي قطع الحديد واحدتها زبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū ʿAmr, and Yaʿqūb read الصدفين with ḍamma; Abū Bakr has ḍamma on ṣād and sukūn on dāl, while others use fatḥa; it refers to the two mountains.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو ويعقوب: بضم الصاد والدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the story, charcoal and wood were placed among the iron pieces before Dhu al-Qarnayn ordered them to blow on the fire.
rows.anchor: وفي القصة: أنه جعل الفحم والحطب في خلال زبر الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The iron became like fire; Dhu al-Qarnayn then called for molten copper, which replaced the burning wood and bonded with the iron.
rows.anchor: أي صار الحديد نارا، {قال آتوني}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza and Abū Bakr connect the hamza in آتوني; the other readers pronounce it with a separated hamza.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة وأبو بكر وصلا وقرأ الآخرون بقطع الألف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qitr means molten copper poured over the iron; the fire consumed the wood and copper took its place, joining to the iron.
rows.anchor: أي: [آتوني قطرا أفرغ عليه، و"الإفراغ": الصب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda compares the barrier to patterned fabric with alternating black and red lines.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هو كالبرد المحبر طريقة سوداء وطريقة حمراء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story gives the barrier's dimensions as fifty cubits wide, two hundred cubits high, and one farsakh long.
rows.anchor: وفي القصة: أن عرضه كان خمسين ذراعا وارتفاعه مائتي ذراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They could not climb over the barrier because it was tall and smooth, or bore through it because it was strong and hard.
rows.anchor: أن يعلوه من فوقه لطوله وملاسته {وما استطاعوا له نقبا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads فما استطاعوا with emphatic ط, assimilating the inflectional t into it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: {فما استطاعوا} بتشديد الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised time may be Judgment Day or the time when Gog and Magog emerge.
rows.anchor: قيل: يوم القيامة وقيل: وقت خروجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kūfan readers use the long, hamzated دكاء, meaning smooth ground; the others read it without lengthening, meaning leveled rubble flush with the earth.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة {دكاء} بالمد والهمز، أي: أرضا ملساء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra, transmitted by Qatāda from Abū Rāfiʿ, says Gog and Magog dig daily until near daylight, then leave and God restores the barrier; eventually their leader says God willing, and they break through.
rows.anchor: وروى قتادة عن أبي رافع عن أبي هريرة يرفعه: "أن يأجوج ومأجوج يحفرونه كل يوم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: In the same report they spread through the land, people take refuge in forts, their arrows return bloodied from the sky, and God kills them with worms in their necks; animals grow fat on their remains.
rows.anchor: فيبعث الله عليهم نغفا في أقفائهم (1) فيهلكون وإن دواب الأرض لتسمن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The report of al-Nawwās ibn Samʿān describes the Dajjāl, urges people to stand firm, and tells anyone who meets him to recite the opening of Sūrat al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه جبير بن نفير عن النواس بن سمعان قال: ذكر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الدجال ذات غداة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Dajjāl emerges between Syria and Iraq; the Prophet calls him a greater fear than the barrier's people and says that, if present, he would contend against him for the believers.
rows.anchor: إن يخرج وأنا فيكم فأنا حجيجه دونكم وإن يخرج ولست فيكم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Dajjāl remains forty days: one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and the rest ordinary days.
rows.anchor: قال: "أربعون يوما يوم كسنة، ويوم كشهر، ويوم كجمعة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When asked whether one prayer suffices during the year-long day, the Prophet says to estimate the prayer times.
rows.anchor: فذلك اليوم الذي كسنة أيكفينا فيه صلاة يوم؟ قال لا اقدروا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view places this at the barrier's opening: Gog and Magog surge into one another like waves of water because of their numbers.
rows.anchor: قيل: هذا عند فتح السد، يقول: تركنا يأجوج ومأجوج يموج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view places it at the Hour, when humans and jinn intermingle in confusion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا عند قيام الساعة، يدخل الخلق بعضهم في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gog and Magog's emergence is a sign that the Hour is near; all people are gathered on one plain.
rows.anchor: لأن خروج يأجوج ومأجوج من علامات قرب الساعة {فجمعناهم جمعا} في صعيد واحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes Hell visible to the unbelievers so they can see it plainly.
rows.anchor: {وعرضنا} أبرزنا {جهنم يومئذ للكافرين عرضا} حتى يشاهدوها عيانا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covering over their eyes is a veil from remembrance, meaning faith and the Qurʾān, guidance and clarification, or the sight of the signs.
rows.anchor: عن ذكري} يعني: عن الإيمان والقرآن، وعن الهدى والبيان.
